study type: Retrospective analysis of a surveillance registry
exposure: Use of extended half-life clotting factor prophylaxis
cohort: The study included 883 infants and toddlers (<=2 years old) with hemophilia A and B, seen at US Hemophilia Treatment Centers and enrolled in the Community Counts Registry.
finding: Intracranial hemorrhage rates in infants and toddlers with hemophilia remain substantial (7.7%), with most initiating prophylaxis within the first year of life, highlighting the need for earlier diagnosis and prophylaxis to prevent ICH.
mod_finding: Known positive family history of hemophilia was associated with decreased rates of vaginal delivery.
